extracted.intended_audience: readers, critics, and writers of travel/colonial accounts (Victorian travel writers and their critics)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards for judging travel writing (especially accounts of colonial peoples and places), emphasizing firsthand observation, accuracy, fairness, and methodological transparency. Focused on how a traveller should gather, report, and qualify claims about other peoples and institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firsthand observation and direct study
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge concerning the mental and moral idiosyncrasies of a people must be acquired directly and at first hand; conclusions should not be drawn when the author has not studied the subjects personally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text criticises Mr. Froude for sitting in a balcony or observing from a ship's deck and yet analysing intimate matters of the people; examples include statements that he 'did not land' yet pronounced characteristics. Advice: land, visit, and gather first-hand impressions rather than generalizing from a distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid one-sided sources / broad sampling of interlocutors
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not base judgments solely on intercourse with a single social group (e.g., 'Anglo‑West Indians'); relying exclusively on one class of witnesses produces a biased, one-sided account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author faults reliance only on 'Anglo‑West Indians' and urges visiting the abodes of Negroes (gentlemen's mansions and peasants' huts alike). Guidance: sample different social, racial, and economic groups when reporting on a society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare and follow a transparent method
rubrics_metrics.description: A trustworthy delineation requires disclosure of the method of inquiry; silence as to method suggests the knowledge was not properly obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The critic notes 'the very silence of the book as to his method ... is a sufficient proof that his knowledge ... has not been acquired directly'; advice: state how observations and information were gathered and what limits exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sweeping generalizations across regions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not assert that 'the characteristics of the people are the same in all the Antilles' or otherwise extrapolate from one locality to an entire region; local differences matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text insists differences of local surroundings and African ancestry produce marked dissimilarities between islands. Guidance: account for local variation and avoid treating distinct colonies as uniform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient time and adequate sampling before judging
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief or cursory visits (e.g., landing only for an afternoon or observing at night from a carriage) are inadequate bases for broad judgments about a people or place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of failing: landing only to dine at a passing resident's house and returning in the dark, then writing paragraphs on the island's character. Guidance: spend adequate time in varied settings and avoid extrapolating from single fleeting experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual accuracy in descriptive detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of objective facts (population figures, tree heights, sanitation, public works) must be accurate; errors on such points undermine the writer's trustworthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The critic highlights implausible details (e.g., 'a cabbage palm a hundred feet high', incorrect population estimates, erroneous sanitary descriptions) as signs of carelessness. Guidance: verify objective claims and numbers before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify hearsay; do not present unverified gossip as fact
rubrics_metrics.description: Maligning or reporting on a people based on hearsay is insufficient; hearsay should not be treated as equivalent to facts elicited by personal investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay accuses the traveller of preferring 'maligning on hearsay' to direct reporting. Guidance: corroborate testimony, seek primary observation, and flag unverified reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid prejudiced, slanderous assertions about groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not make hideous slanders or sweeping derogatory claims (for example, about marriage practices or social worth) about large social or racial groups when ignorant of the facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The critic condemns statements such as 'no white girl will marry a Negro' and the suggestion that daughters of educated coloured folk 'will not marry among their own people' as 'hideous slander'. Guidance: avoid demeaning generalisations and check cultural claims carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not impute motives without evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid asserting ulterior motives for individuals or political movements (e.g., that reform leaders only want large salaries) unless supported by evidence; imputing motives is slanderous if unfounded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author calls the claim about Reform leaders' motives 'not criticism: it is slander.' Guidance: distinguish proven fact from speculation about motive and present supporting evidence when claiming motives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness, balance, and avoidance of partisan sneer
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain even-handedness; do not dismiss political movements or local claims with flippant sneers or contempt without engaging the substantive grievances or evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The critic objects to Mr. Froude's 'flippant sneer' at reformers and insists on allowing legitimate claims their scope. Guidance: present opposing viewpoints respectfully and consider local political context before condemning movements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resist rhetorical licence that sacrifices accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Vivid or picturesque language must not trump factual precision; alternating ecstatic praise and groundless detraction undermines credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text notes Mr. Froude's habit of 'blowing hot and cold' and 'luxuriating in his contempt for exactitude.' Guidance: balance literary flourish with careful checking of facts and consistent judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid extrapolating social character from material goods alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Inferring a people's character from signs of comfort or domestic furnishings seen fleetingly (e.g., armchairs, cut-glass) is unreliable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The critic ridicules drawing long conclusions from a nocturnal carriage view of houses with engravings; guidance: avoid deriving broad cultural or intellectual judgments from isolated material observations.
